title: Irrational cubic fourfolds with geometric K3 categories
main_claim: There is an ineffective d0 such that for every admissible Hassett discriminant d > d0, a very general cubic fourfold in C_d is irrational even though Ku(X) is equivalent to D^b(S) for a K3 surface S. This would disprove Kuznetsov's conjecture. The proof evaluates one divisorial invariant c_u(f) of a hypothetical map f: P^4 --> X in two ways. Weak factorization plus a Gromov-Witten operator algebra that tracks whole integral surface-transcendental blocks gives c_u = 1. A Sarkisov factorization with uniformly bounded link diagrams and an intrinsic correction v+s that telescopes gives c_u = 0.

issues.location: sections/gw.tex, Theorem gw:blowup / Lemmas gw:relative, gw:divisor
issues.description: The claim that G_Y = G_M (+) Q id_W with zero mixed blocks (no genus-zero GW operator connecting T_M and an exceptional T_Z block, even when they are Hodge-isometric) is new and load-bearing. It is proved by a multi-layer induction on the degeneration formula. I checked the dimension and Hodge-type bookkeeping and the base cases, and I tried a test case: a section-type surface inside an earlier exceptional divisor. There the virtual-dimension count gives vanishing. I found no failing step, but the tensor-level triangularity of B_abs = C*B_rel + R across all graph types could not be fully verified. Treat this as residual risk, not a gap.
issues.evidence: 'G_Y=G_M\oplus\Q\,\operatorname{id}_{T_Z}' ... 'We have an identity B_abs = C B_rel + R, with C in Q^* independent of the two variable vectors.'

issues.description: The uniform boundedness of the marked contraction diagrams (vertices, graphs, exceptional and bad loci) in families of Fano-type pairs rests on [CLZ26], Choi-Li-Zhou 2026, Theorems 1.2-1.7. I could not check this against the source. Every 'sufficiently large d' threshold in Sections 4-6 depends on it.

coverage:
I read all seven sections of the LaTeX source in full: introduction, preliminaries, gw, bounds, surface-links, subfields and cubics. Checks I made:
- Preliminaries: the cocycle additivity and blow-up signs, and the MRC test.
- Lemma gw:k3-center: the Noether/Euler computation b2 = 22 - 8q - K^2, the Picard-rank-one argument, and the automorphism glue argument (needs d > 2).
- Lemma gw:blocks / gw:net-center: block bookkeeping via primitive central idempotents.
- K3 pencil bound: 2g - 2 >= n*sqrt(d).
- Bounded-MRC degree bound: d <= A^2 + (A.K)^2.
- Exclusions (i)-(iv) and Riemann-Hurwitz.
- Vertical/horizontal decomposition: the tower identity v(V/Q) = v - h_Q + v(B/Q), v(B/Q) = 0, and the residual formula.
- Low-base cases (dim Q = 0, 1, 3) and the generic-surface dichotomy.
- Conic h_Q = -u(Delta).
- Two-ray table for two divisorial ends: recomputed with Python, and it matches exactly.
- One-divisorial-end list (a,e) and |Delta| = 8 - D.
- Star/triangle bijection P_Delta = E + E.
- Pencil-set identifications in degrees 5 and 6, including the C3/S3 argument for (4,2,2).
- Eligibility, the uniqueness argument and conic-end vanishing via first-departure log links.
- The ordering of the coefficient c relative to the d threshold.
- Telescoping in Theorem sf:vanishing.
- Application to C_d: very general lattice data, Voisin's CH_0 corollary, and the admissibility arithmetic for 2n^2+2n+2 and 2*7^j.

I followed the deep GW degeneration induction and the cited boundedness results (Birkar BAB, CLZ26, HM13) only at the level of logic and hypotheses. I did not re-derive them.
